exile.excerpt: There was once a King who had three sons, and he had also a stepdaughter. They all lived together in peace and happiness and had everything their hearts could desire. But after a time an enemy of the King came against him with a great army, and slew him, and took the kingdom and drove forth the Princes into the world, and their stepsister with them.
exile.note: Verbatim text from Katherine Pyle's 1922 English children's retelling. The collection labels it Lithuanian but does not identify an oral informant or underlying source text.

narrativeBlocks.title: A king loses his kingdom
narrativeBlocks.body: In Katherine Pyle's story labeled Lithuanian, an enemy kills the king, takes the kingdom, and drives the three princes and their stepsister into the world.

narrativeBlocks.title: Four travelers leave together
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from Pyle's English retelling (whitespace normalized): “There was once a King who had three sons, and he had also a stepdaughter. They all lived together in peace and happiness and had everything their hearts could desire. But after a time an enemy of the King came against him with a great army, and slew him, and took the kingdom and drove forth the Princes into the world, and their stepsister with them.”

narrativeBlocks.title: A retold story begins
narrativeBlocks.body: The collection frames the text as a Lithuanian story, but does not identify a specific oral informant or an earlier source edition for this tale.

narrativeBlocks.title: A modern English retelling
narrativeBlocks.body: Katherine Pyle's 1922 Fairy Tales from Far and Near includes stories explicitly labeled by region. This is a children's literary retelling, not a direct translation of a named Lithuanian manuscript.

narrativeBlocks.title: Limit the claim to this tale
narrativeBlocks.body: This lesson follows one Lithuanian-labeled story in Pyle's collection; it is not a complete survey of Baltic mythology or folklore.
